### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8dd8192cbfb35dddc4f38f228edc1fb62c909ad3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1d3f0d4a9c17de87ed189c37f5af2298d721efc0` — the merge of head `3b8da3efcece663102807c87c3fc38c876e236f1` into base `8dd8192cbfb35dddc4f38f228edc1fb62c909ad3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1d3f0d4a9c17de87ed189c37f5af2298d721efc0 && git checkout 1d3f0d4a9c17de87ed189c37f5af2298d721efc0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8dd8192cbfb35dddc4f38f228edc1fb62c909ad3 3b8da3efcece663102807c87c3fc38c876e236f1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8dd8192cbfb35dddc4f38f228edc1fb62c909ad3 && git merge --no-ff 3b8da3efcece663102807c87c3fc38c876e236f1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8dd8192cbfb35dddc4f38f228edc1fb62c909ad3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

The body's local readings name `978472fc`; the report and final-head comment 6938023419 give the same counts on this head.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3b8da3efcece663102807c87c3fc38c876e236f1`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/engine-insert.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-validate.ts, packages/objectql/src/summary-batch-accumulation.ts, packages/objectql/src/summary-batch-accumulation.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/summary-rollup.test.ts + read in the cited code, not reviewed: packages/objectql/src/master-detail.ts (`resolveMasterDetailRelation`), packages/objectql/src/engine-references-and-master-detail.ts (`resolveMasterDetailParents`, `materializeParentHeader`), packages/objectql/src/engine-master-detail-related.ts (`resolvePreviewParents`, `resolvePredicateRelated`), packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts (`masterIdOf`), packages/objectql/src/engine-summaries-and-expansion.ts (descriptor construction), packages/objectql/src/summary-rule-reads.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts and content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx on `main`. Prose faces not reviewed: content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx, .changeset/34466-batch-insert-parent-summary-predicate.md (read for ② only).

Inputs read: card #34466 body and all 5 comments; PR #34612 body, 7-file list, 3 comments and the net diff against merge-base `8dd8192c`; ruling record 6928862195 on #33795 in full; #25579 body and all 4 comments (ruling 6377847361 letter C as restated there, dev report 6442152067); the 53 check-runs on this head.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set, the narrowing (right, and it is the only one). Subject: a detail object with exactly one `master_detail` relation, a field-level `requiredWhen` that reads `parent.SUMMARY`, where SUMMARY is a roll-up of the header over that detail object with function `count`, or `sum` / `min` / `max` over number values, and a filter that names no dotted path. Writes: `insert(object, rows[])` and `insertMany` with more than one row (so the generic batch create and the import's batched creates). Before: every row of the batch judged the header as read once before the batch, so a later row was admitted without the field the predicate requires. Now: each row judges the stored summary moved by the earlier rows of the same batch that passed the whole admit step, so the row one-by-one inserts refuse is refused: `insert(array)` rejects the whole batch with `VALIDATION_FAILED` (field, `required`), `insertMany` answers that row `ok: false` and writes the others. The opposite direction also exists and is right for the same reason: a predicate that turns false as the summary grows (for example required only while the header has no line) now stops requiring the field on later rows, as one by one does. That is a widening of what one batch admits; it follows from the same rule and needs no second declaration, but the changeset names only the refusing direction (nit N4).
- Accept-set, the preview (right). `validate` with `mode: 'insert'` and more than one row answers the same per-row verdicts as the write, for the same subject. Not moved in `update` mode: the accumulator is created for `mode === 'insert'` only.
- Not moved, checked in the code and each right: a single-row insert (no accumulator under `rows.length` of 1); an update; a `parent.` predicate reading a header field that is no summary (the patch touches only `desc.summaryField`); an unbound header (`null` / `undefined` returned as is, so the fail-closed signal of an unreadable or missing header survives); an object with two masters (`resolveMasterDetailRelation` answers `null`, no header is bound at all, as before); `avg`, a non-number value, a dotted-path filter (dropped by the accumulator, the stored value stands); a header of another id or another object.
- Refactor, `overlay()` (right). Its per-row body moved to `patchRow` unchanged: same descriptor filter (`dropped`, `parentObject`), same key test (`summaryField in row`), same `moved` arithmetic, same copy-on-write. The reference arm of #25579 does not move. Its 11 existing unit pins and the #25579 engine pins are in the green Test Core shards.
- Public surface: `BatchSummaryAccumulator` gains `overlayRow`. The module is engine-internal (imported by `engine-insert.ts` and `engine-validate.ts` only); no export of `@objectstack/objectql`, no schema, no contract member, no error code changes shape. The refusal is the existing `ValidationError` envelope.
- Order and authority (right, nothing skipped or reordered). The diff adds no await and no read. The header is still read by `resolveMasterDetailParents`: the caller's read door first, then the tenant-kept elevated read for the headers that door returned. `insertParentOf` only wraps the per-row lookup in a synchronous copy. The reference check still runs before the rules for a non-system write and after them for a system write, and `accept` still runs after both, so a row refused for a reference the caller cannot read, for its shape, for its currency code, or by a rule is never counted. The value added to the header is derived from the caller's own batch rows alone; no stored value reaches a caller that did not already feed this predicate.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/objectql` is the right level: `Metadata-protocol: none` is right (no key, accepted value or requirement on what a metadata author can write changes; what moves is a runtime verdict on data rows), and AGENTS.md ships a non-protocol breaking change as `patch` with its BREAKING banner. Same level and shape as the precedent PR #26680.
- The changeset carries both declaration lines, the BREAKING banner, FROM and TO, the one-line fix for a caller, and one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), which fits: no stored row or authored value is rewritten. `Check Changeset` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` conclude success on this head.
- Clause-②: no (narrowing). Agreed: nothing published widens in shape, and a batch admitted before can now be refused. The PR body and the changeset carry the same line.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on this head: 53, all completed; 38 success, 15 skipped, none failed, none pending. Read as the gate verdicts: Build Core, Test Core 1 to 8 of 8, TypeScript Type Check and its four parts, Lint and Repo Gates and its parts, Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Build Docs, Live E2E UI all success. For the seat: the CI dogfood shards (`Dogfood Regression Gate` matrix) and the Test UI shards are among the skipped jobs on this head, and their aggregate jobs conclude success over the skip. The full dogfood battery a declared narrowing owes (rule card #34424) therefore rests on the dev's local reading in report 6938005588, which this review did not and may not re-run. Whether that reading satisfies the battery rule is the lane seat's call, not a finding on the diff.
- Dev deviation 1 (engine-validate.ts and one docs sentence outside the first claim surface): answered. The area added both in comment 6935662127 before the PR, and changing the preview with the write is what keeps the dry run honest (#25579 did the same).
- Dev deviation 2 (PR body readings name `978472fc`): answered. The head is a merge of `main` into `978472fc`; the net diff against the merge-base is the 7 files above, and the check-runs judged this head.
- Dev deviation 3 (no review request call): process only, the seat's.
- `open_questions`: one, the route to this review; answered by this record.
- `out_of_scope_findings`: the predicate update (`multi: true`) has the same pre-batch header; carried by #34465, not touched here, correctly.
- `security_findings: none`: agreed on the diff, see ① order and authority. No possible access finding.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no finding. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no per-row re-read. The accumulation is in memory because the rows it counts are not written yet, so no SQL aggregate could see them; ruling 6377847361 as claimed on #25579 fixes that shape ("accumulated in memory per batch, never re-queried per row"), and the module header states it.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes the published rule real; it takes no declared capability away. The spec on `main` declares the header as `parent` for a field-level predicate (`field.zod.ts`), and the published docs on `main` state "A bulk create equals one-by-one creates" under ruling 6377847361, which ruling record 6928862195 restates and lists this exact case as the open gap ("A multi-row insert does not accumulate for a field-level `parent.` predicate that reads a parent summary"). No published line promises that a batch reads the pre-batch header for a rule; the one such promise on `main` is for hooks and flow steps, which this diff leaves alone. `summary-rule-reads.ts` class (ii) already names the field such a predicate reads, so the card's first Done-when arm applies and the docs-limit arm is correctly not taken.

Attempts to break it, each read in the code at this head:

- Mixed parents in one batch: deltas are keyed per descriptor and per parent id, and the header lookup is per row; `masterIdOf` and `singleId` reduce a string or number key to the same string. Holds; pinned (two headers, two lines each).
- A row refused mid-batch: a row culled before the loop is skipped, and a row that throws anywhere in the admit step never reaches `accept`. Holds; pinned (second row refused, third reads one earlier line).
- Filtered summary: the filter is judged on the new row by the aggregation's own walker before the row is counted, unchanged code shared with the reference arm. Holds.
- A row whose header the caller cannot read: the header binds `null`, `overlayRow` returns it as is, and the reference check refuses the row before it can be counted. Holds.
- A rule that reads the same summary through the reference and a `requiredWhen` that reads it on `parent`: both arms read one accumulator, so they agree within a row. Holds.
- Deferred recompute scope around an insert: class (ii) keeps a summary this predicate reads out of the deferral, so the stored base is current between calls. Holds.
- Nested summaries and derived header fields: see N1.
- A row admitted and then lost: see N2.
- The preview on a withheld column: see N3.

Tests against the card: the Done-when asks for a pinned case plus a CONTROL reading a non-summary header field. The engine pins use three rows where the third is the first one refused, on the real engine and recompute, with the one-by-one reference answer beside them, the atomic and per-row doors, the preview, the per-header split and the `parent.status` CONTROL; the unit pins cover the copy and the four leave-as-is cases. The ablation the dev reports (four red, the rest green) is the lane's account; the pins as written would behave so.

Findings:

- N1 (nit) — follow-up card, no change on this head. The overlay moves the summary field only. A header field derived from it (a formula, or a stored expression field such as "is full when line_count is at least 2") still reads its pre-batch value inside one batch, where one by one it is re-derived after each recompute; the same holds for a summary of a summary one level up. The docs and changeset claim only the direct `parent.SUMMARY` read, so nothing published is false, and the card's scope is that read. The bulk-update arm already closes this by its read closure; the bulk-create arm (reference and `parent` alike) does not, and no card carries it.
- N2 (nit) — accepted deviation, inherited from #25579. `accept` runs when the rules admit a row. Under `insertMany` a row that is then lost to a later step of the same write (an autonumber issue failure) stays counted for later rows, so a later row can be refused where one by one would admit it. #25579's report 6442152067 noted the same for the reference arm, "not filed"; the published sentence says "rows the rules admitted", which the code matches. A driver write failure rejects the whole batch, so it leaves no survivor to misjudge.
- N3 (nit) — accepted deviation or one prose sentence. In the preview a header column the read door withheld from the caller reads `null`, and `moved` treats `null` as the empty set, so later rows of the preview read the batch's own count (0 plus the batch) where the write reads stored plus the batch. No stored value flows to the caller, and it agrees with the preview's standing rule that a withheld column is judged as empty; the preview and the write already differed on such a column before this diff.
- N4 (nit) — prose face only. The changeset's BREAKING block describes the refusing direction; a predicate that relaxes as the summary grows now admits later rows it used to refuse in one batch. One sentence in the changeset would name it.

No must-fix, no should-fix.
